official_measurement_examples: local plans must be accompanied by a policies map
site allocations show land identified for a particular development use
draft allocation and adopted allocation are different statuses
HELAA inclusion does not itself create an allocation
a policies-map boundary visualises policy application but is not ownership geometry
2026 site-selection guidance uses staged identification assessment draft allocation and confirmation
new-style local-plan examination guidance applies to plans submitted on or after 31 December 2026
site allocation does not itself grant planning permission or final development yield
core_rules: draft allocation is not adopted allocation
adopted allocation is not planning permission
policies map is not cadastral title map
emerging policy weight is not adopted-policy weight
site allocation does not guarantee delivery
site allocation does not establish ownership
site allocation does not establish access rights
allocation does not discharge environmental consents
allocation does not prove utility capacity
policies-map symbology is not legal extent evidence beyond the plan
legacy and new plan systems must remain distinct
superseded allocation is not current allocation
no parcel allocation clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official MHCLG/GOV.UK, Planning Inspectorate, legislation and current English local-plan sources checked 2026-07-26. 2026 site-selection/new-system transition and draft-versus-adopted allocation distinctions retained; no parcel promotion.
